what_happened: Research found the full relay plumbing (user_decision -> postflight -> Move3/Move4) is already generic and complete, and a near-identical hand-off precedent (push-consent-relay.md) already exists to copy; task's own pre-research proposed_file_scope (skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, orchestrate-record-decision.sh) is not needed -- narrows the implementing plan's footprint to books agent definitions only.

The exact absent-or-stale failure signature for check-approvals.sh/full-gate.sh (the component gate's approvals leg) lives only in the companion Logos/Verification repository, not readable from this session; the detection rule's literal marker text cannot be pinned by this research and must be read directly during planning.

Research flagged the absent-or-stale failure signature as unreadable (Logos/Verification is a separate repository). During planning the scripts were found locally at /home/benjamin/Projects/Logos/Verification/components/framed_channel/{scripts/check-approvals.sh,check.sh}, so the literal signature was pinned from source rather than guessed, removing the plan's single named blocking unknown.

Plan Step 5.1 instructed deploying and confirming the new books-extension files under .claude/, but the books extension is not loaded in this repository's .claude-extensions.json, so deploy-headless.sh deploys nothing for it. Pre-existing repository condition, not caused by this task; worked around by demonstrating the relay via core's own deployed orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh instead, which is extension-agnostic.

A bare 'approve.sh' mention in the books implementation agents' MUST NOT lists tripped check-extension-docs.sh Rule E (check_referenced_scripts_declared). Fixed by adding approve.sh to the books extension's manifest.json external_scripts array, the same escape hatch the approvals extension's own manifest already uses.

The 76-case forgery-probed fixture suite for books-approvals-signal.sh, including structural assertions over both books implementation agents with their own forgery probes, passed clean on first full run after two small false-positive fixes to the self-check predicates themselves (quote-stripping for the no-self-answering check; known-safe-redirection stripping for the write-redirection check).
